bibliographic.title: A survey on augmenting knowledge graphs (KGs) with large language models (LLMs): models, evaluation metrics, benchmarks, and challenges
bibliographic.authors: Nourhan Ibrahim; Samar Aboulela; Ahmed Ibrahim; Rasha Kashef
bibliographic.citation_apa: Ibrahim, N., Aboulela, S., Ibrahim, A., & Kashef, R. (2024). A survey on augmenting knowledge graphs (KGs) with large language models (LLMs): models, evaluation metrics, benchmarks, and challenges. Discover Artificial Intelligence, 4, 76. https://doi.org/10.1007/s44163-024-00175-8

methodology.sample_description: key papers from NLP, machine learning, and knowledge representation gathered to understand KG-LLM integration approaches in the last decade
methodology.technology_context: KG-augmented LLMs, LLM-augmented KGs, synergized frameworks, RAG, evaluation metrics and benchmarks

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article is a peer-reviewed survey on KG-LLM integration with explicit RAG and interpretability content, which is peripherally relevant to knowledge-base and retrieval governance in LLM systems. The provided text does not address conversational governance, human oversight, accountability, audit, compliance, guardrails, or regulated-domain operational controls, so it is not central evidence for the review scope.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only front matter and partial methodology are available; full paper needed to confirm absence of governance, oversight, and regulated-context operational content beyond introductory industry mentions.

appraisal.notes: Clear survey objective and stated multi-phase systematic review methodology with three-paradigm classification and comparative framework. Sample size, search strategy details, ethics, and full limitations are not evidenced in the excerpt provided.

cerqual.explanation: The study is internally coherent as a technical survey of KG-LLM integration paradigms, but adequacy of sampling and direct relevance to conversational governance in regulated environments are limited based on the text provided.

synthesis.main_claim: Integrating LLMs with knowledge graphs enhances interpretability and performance of AI systems, and integration approaches can be classified into three paradigms with distinct methodologies, strengths, drawbacks, and applications.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a structured survey taxonomy (KG-augmented LLMs, LLM-augmented KGs, synergized frameworks), discusses evaluation metrics and benchmarks, and identifies challenges such as scalability and computational overhead.
synthesis.limitations: The provided text notes challenges including scalability and computational overhead, but full study limitations are unclear from the excerpt.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting technical background for RAG, knowledge-base integration, and interpretability in LLM systems; not suitable as central evidence for conversational governance, oversight, audit, or compliance in regulated settings.
